article_text:
ファッションはフリーズ・ロンドンを「俗化」させたのか？ フェアに押し寄せる業界人たちの功罪

フリーズ・ロンドン の会場に、奇抜な装いに身を包んだ ファッション 業界人が大挙して押し寄せている。セルフィー目当ての彼らに対し、アート界からは冷ややかな声が上がる一方、ファッションとの接近はフェアに経済的な恩恵ももたらしてもいる。

ロンドンのフリーズ・ウィークは、いまやファッション業界人にとっての「聖地巡礼」の場だ。2022年以降、 ファッション 関係者がアートフェアに大挙して押し寄せるようになり、同年には アレキサンダー・マックイーン とロクサンダ・イリンチック（Roksanda Ilinčić）が、 フリーズ・ロンドン （Frieze London）とフリーズ・マスターズ（Frieze Masters）の開催に合わせてランウェイショーを実施した。今年のフリーズ・ウィークでは、開催前から、インスタグラム用の写真を撮るためだけに会場へ立ち寄るファッション関係者が増えていることがアートジャーナリストや広報担当者、ギャラリストの間で話題になっていた。

では、ファッションはフリーズを俗化させてしまったのだろうか？

「台無しにしたとまでは言いませんが、セルフィーを撮ることに夢中なファッション女子があまりにも増えたことで、フリーズでの体験の価値が多少なりとも損なわれたとは思います。そういう私自身も、セルフィー好きのファッション女子なんですけどね」

UK版VOGUEのファッション＆スタイルエディター、マホロ・スワードはUS版ARTnewsの取材にこう語った。

VIPプレビュー（今年は10月14日に開催）は、いまでは著名人が一堂に会する社交の場となっている。今年の来場者には、俳優のティルダ・スウィントンやモニカ・バルバロ、ファッションデザイナーのラフ・シモンズやドリス・ヴァン・ノッテン、そして ジョン・ガリアーノ によるZARAのコレクションをまとったビアンカ・ジャガーらが名を連ねた。こうした人々の装いは、もはや「衣装」と呼びたくなるほどコンセプチュアルになっている（展示作品以上にコンセプチュアルかもしれない）。革やファー、スパンコールをまとった人々に加え、蒸し暑いテントの中では、お揃いのPVC製キャットスーツに身を包んだ2人組が闊歩していた。

ロンドン・ファッション・ウィークなら、こうした奇抜な装いはストリートスナップのカメラマンたちから喝采を浴びるだろう。しかし、フリーズでは冷ややかな視線を向けられる。

「ファッション業界では、恥じらいがなければないほど称賛されます。彼らは、自分たちの業界そのものを見せ物にしてしまったのです」

匿名を条件に取材に応じたあるファッションエディターは語る。もちろん、アート業界の人々が着飾ったり服装で自己表現したりすることを好まないわけではない。ただ、その装いはたいてい、イッセイミヤケのプリーツプリーズや、 エルメス の端正なコートやハンドバッグ「エヴリン」といったものだ。

一方、フリーズのフェア担当エグゼクティブ・ディレクター、クリステル・シャデのように、「参加者は多ければ多いほどいい」という立場の人もいる。ファッション業界が積極的に関わることは、フリーズにとっても参加ギャラリーにとっても経済的なメリットがあるというのがシャデの主張だ。2023年には、ストーンアイランド（Stone Island）がフリーズ・ロンドンのパートナーとなり、新進ギャラリー34軒に助成金を提供。一方、ダンヒル（Dunhill）はフリーズ・マスターズとの初のパートナーシップを開始した。シャデはこう語る。

「フリーズは、多様な声や異なる分野が交わるプラットフォームです。そうした豊かさと多様性こそが、このフェアを唯一無二のものにしていると思います」

こうした動きに注目するブランドは、さらに増えている。 ティファニー は昨年から、フリーズの「アーティスト・トゥ・アーティスト」プログラムのパートナーを務めており、 ロエベ もフリーズ・ロンドンのVIPプログラムを支援している（ちなみに、フェアの会場マップを兼ねたパンフレットの裏表紙に、美しいロエベのキャンペーンビジュアルが掲載されているのは気分がいい）。

「とはいえ」と、前出のスワードは続ける。

「フリーズがそれほど神聖な場所だとも思いません。もちろん、批評的に高く評価されるべき素晴らしい作品が展示されていますが、根本的には商業的な場ですから」

ファッション業界によるアート界への進出は、戦略的な動きでもある。ブランド各社が狙っているのは、フリーズ・マスターズに出展した ハウザー＆ワース のブースで、 ヤン・ブリューゲル（父） の《Still Life of Flowers in a Stoneware Vase》（1607〜08年）に600万ドル（約9億5000万円）以上を投じるような富裕層の消費者だ。消費者が支出に慎重になり、売り上げ減少という課題に直面しているラグジュアリーファッションブランドは、相次いで価格を引き上げている。ファッション業界がF1や全米オープンテニス、そしてフリーズ・ロンドンといった場に進出しているのは、こうした事情があるからだ。

ロクサンダ・イリンチックが2023年春夏コレクションのショーをフリーズ・ロンドン開幕前夜に開催したのも、同じ理由からだった。当時、彼女は筆者にこう語っている。

「私のブランドの顧客には、アートやクリエイティブな分野に関わる人がとても多いんです。それは素晴らしいことですし、実際、顧客のかなりの割合を占めています。普段はショーに来られない方も多いのですが、今回はフリーズのために皆さんロンドンに集まっているので、お会いできるのがとても嬉しいです」

イリンチックはまた、「ファッションは、あらゆるものに関わろうとします。スポーツ、アート、演劇、ハリウッドでも、同じ現象を目にしてきました。ファッションは、それ自体がひとつの強大な力なのです」とも述べている。

ファッションのこうした力を認めるのは、『Ace: The Times & Style of Tennis』（Abrams Books、2026年）の著者、スニータ・クマール・ナイア（Sunita Kumar Nair）だ。ナイアは著書の中で、ファッションが「トロイの木馬」のようにテニス界へ入り込んでいった過程を考察しており、アート界でも同じ構図が生まれつつあると見ている。彼女はこう語る。

「ファッションは自然の力のようなものです。行き過ぎれば、破壊することもあれば、何かを生み出すこともあります。私にとって、テニスとファッションの関係について書くことは、ごく自然な切り口でした。ファッションの人気の高さを考えれば、避けては通れないテーマだと思ったのです」

フリーズでの体験が損なわれた責任をファッション関係者に押し付けるのは不公平かもしれない。しかし、インスタグラムをざっと眺めれば、真っ先に自分たちの存在をアピールしているのが彼らであることは明らかだ。

あるベテランのファッション広報担当者は、「フリーズでの様子を投稿することは、壁に『ここに来た』と落書きするのと同じ、新しい自己主張の方法になっています」という。

もっとも、バレンシアガをまとって気取って歩き回り、ルイナールのシャンパン片手に、ファション業界お決まりのエアキスを交わしたところで、罪に問われるわけではない。少なくとも、今のところは。（翻訳：編集部）

title_original: Making Marie Antoinette Review: A Celebration of Creative Collaboration
editorial_title_zh: 《制造玛丽·安托瓦内特》影评：对创意合作的礼赞
editorial_excerpt_zh: 注：本影评最初作为我们报道2026年纽约电影节（NYFF）的内容发表。该片将于10月23日登陆院线，11月6日上线MUBI。在这部由索菲亚·科波拉（Sofia Coppola）执导、绚丽辉煌且带有时代错置感的影片中，视觉上的流光溢彩、奢华优雅与繁复装饰包裹着的……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "注：本影评最初作为我们报道2026年纽约电影节（NYFF）的内容发表。该片将于10月23日登陆院线，11月6日上线MUBI。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://thefilmstage.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/tfs-criticspick-star-orange.png", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "The Film Stage", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在这部由索菲亚·科波拉（Sofia Coppola）执导、绚丽辉煌且带有时代错置感的影片《玛丽·安托瓦内特》中，包裹着的是一个年轻女子离开家人去协助领导另一个国家的故事——这是一段未知的旅程，也是一份财富、过度及其令人沮丧的孤立的同步记录。然而，尽管科波拉触及了她短暂的电影作品中反复出现的主题，但至少在片场，她从未面临过与其命运多舛的女主角相同的分离与孤独。这在很大程度上是因为她的母亲埃莉诺·科波拉（Eleanor Coppola）一直陪伴在她身旁——在凡尔赛宫的大厅里，用她的数码相机潜行、观察并记录下了80个小时的幕后素材。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "埃莉诺将这些素材搁置了14年，随后在疫情期间与索菲亚一同将其重新翻找出来，希望能将这些个人素材转化为一部档案纪录片。如今，在埃莉诺去世两周年（以及《玛丽·安托瓦内特》上映20周年）之际，索菲亚完成了母亲的愿景。剪辑师亚伦·马修斯（Aaron Matthews）对埃莉诺的数码资料库进行了梳理和剪辑——这些素材完全捕捉自该片长达57天的拍摄期——并赋予其鲜活的生命力。相比电子新闻资料包，这部影片更具转瞬即逝的质感和叙事考量，并浸润着母亲本能的、欣赏的、鼓励的目光。《制造玛丽·安托瓦内特》既是一部引人入胜的时间胶囊，记录了一位年轻电影人寻找自我声音的过程，也是一次难得的幕后窥探，让我们得以一窥这部最初被误解、如今已拥有Criterion 4K修复版的经典之作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "或许正因如此，埃莉诺决定徘徊在《玛丽·安托瓦内特》的边缘，并不是她最自然的状态。距离她联合执导、广受赞誉的1991年纪录片《黑暗之心：电影人的末日》（关于她丈夫拍摄《现代启示录》幕后）已经过去15年了，但这一次，她带着惊人的自我审视态度走近了镜头。交织在女儿出众的电影制作才华集锦之中的，是埃莉诺的日记摘录（由黛安·莱恩[Diane Lane]配音），她在其中反思了自己作为创意工作者的地位，并质疑自己是否配得上举起相机。“我基本上是一个害羞的人，讨厌打扰别人，”她说。“拍摄纪录片违背了我的性格。然而，一次又一次，我还是这么做了。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种犹豫不决以及埃莉诺对自身干涉的觉察，出人意料地赋予了她更为亲密的视角。她静静地博取正在为一场戏做准备的克尔斯滕·邓斯特（Kirsten Dunst）的好感，倾听处理后勤问题的制片人之间的私下对话，并发现自己离得足够近，能够捕捉到那些更为主动、更具指导性的纪录片导演可能会错过的微小、毫无防备的时刻——比如杰森·舒瓦兹曼（Jason Schwartzman）摆弄大键琴时的搞怪。就像看到广为流传的表情包背后的原始素材一样，通过埃莉诺的镜头重新审视某些标志性的幕后剧照（即邓斯特和舒瓦兹曼专注地看着MacBook），既充满启发性又令人感到新奇，闲聊、笑声和背景音乐为其注入了活力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如同最好的幕后纪录片，《制造玛丽·安托瓦内特》特别旨在突出工作中的匠心。这里有大量的素材可看，首先是服装设计师米莱娜·卡农诺罗（Milena Canonero），她为邓斯特设计了72套独一无二的礼服。更不用说为其他所有演员和群众演员配备各自特定时代服装、妆容和假发的繁重任务了，这些造型每天都需要清洗和扑粉。片中有一幕，一位助理指出，制作组每周都会因为这些准备时间而损失整整一天，这让人清楚地看到，索菲亚不仅是在执导一部古装剧情片，更是在统筹一整支部门主管和协调人员的队伍，他们的执行和临场调整必须以精确的方式保持一致，才能使这场制作顺利运作。这是一副沉重的担负，但在记录一座从不向电影拍摄敞开大门的宫殿内部所需的手工劳作、僵硬预算和残酷日程时，埃莉诺提醒着我们，电影制作在多大程度上依赖于那些神秘的特质：合作与协作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管这些截然不同的部分能够汇聚到一起并保持制作进度让人感觉像是个奇迹，但埃莉诺同样清醒地意识到那些紧张的时刻——在这些时刻中，索菲亚必须提高嗓音，在混乱中维持其愿景。“我觉得我被排除在那次讨论之外了，”她对一个解释为什么群众演员还没为一场戏做好准备的人说道。起初，这可能看起来像是一种胆怯却又带点被动攻击的反应，但它是一个极具教育意义的提醒，让我们看到了索菲亚不断置身的那个由男性主导的空间——这是一个具有讽刺意味的并置，因为影片的大部分时间都是在女性陪伴下度过的，她们穿着糖果色衣裙、顶着高耸的发型吃着水果和巧克力。拍摄进入后期，仿佛急于展示女儿在片场自身的成长，埃莉诺巧妙地偷听了索菲亚与她的摄影师之间的另一次温和对峙。这一次，导演对摄像机视角应始终跟随其主角的立场采取了更为坚定的态度。“这不是那个男人的故事，”她说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如果这些互动捕捉到了索菲娅在片场可能感受到的某些紧张，那么还有更多的互动反映了包围着日常制作的美丽与轻松。在许多方面，《绝代艳后》都是一场家庭事务——从索菲娅的哥哥罗曼（Roman）开始，他空降拍摄第二组镜头，并为索菲娅提供了另一双眼睛。甚至还有几天，她的父亲弗朗西斯（Francis）也来了，在众说纷纭中，他有效地赋予了女儿继续为自己的愿景抗争的许可。“办一场《绝代艳后》派对，把所有人都请来，”他建议道。“按你想要的方式去做。”但这些间断的援助与埃莉诺对索菲娅无处不在的陪伴相比，就显得黯然失色了。在制作初期，她注意到索菲娅日益严重的感冒，并最终找来医生诊断她的支气管炎。后来，在玛丽和她母亲的一场戏中，埃莉诺巧妙地将镜头向左平移，捕捉到索菲娅透过摄影机观看的画面，意识到了正在上演的某种关系上的呼应。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在兼顾埃莉诺的情感与反思的同时，从不牺牲其所记录制作的节奏与时间线，《制作〈绝代艳后〉》将最具洞察力的魅力留到了最后。关于创作过程的最佳纪录片能激发并滋生创作的渴望。显然，仅仅是电影制作的过程本身就重新焕发了埃莉诺内心的艺术生命（尽管它具有讽刺意味地让索菲娅重新考虑是否还要再拍一部如此昂贵的电影）。“难道我不应该投入到我自己的创作过程中，而不仅仅是观察我才华横溢的家人的作品吗？”她问道。十年后，她用行动回答了那个内心的疑问，凭借2016年的《巴黎任我行》（Paris Can Wait）成为以剧情长片导演处女作亮相的最年长的女性。正是这种圆满的时刻，让这部纪录片感觉就像是找到了一块久违的拼图，并将其卡入其色彩斑斓、紧密相连的位置。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《制作〈绝代艳后〉》在第64届纽约电影节上进行了展映，并将于10月23日登陆院线，于11月6日上线MUBI。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Note: This review was originally published as part of our 2026 NYFF coverage. The film arrives in theaters on October 23 and on MUBI on November 6."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://thefilmstage.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/tfs-criticspick-star-orange.png", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "The Film Stage"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Wrapped inside the visual splendor, luxurious elegance, and ornate decoration of Sofia Coppola’s resplendent and anachronistic Marie Antoinette is the story of a young woman leaving her family behind to help lead another country—an unknown journey and simultaneous document of wealth, excess, and its depressive isolation. Yet despite Coppola tapping into her short filmography’s recurring themes, at least on set, she never contended with the same separation and loneliness of her ill-fated heroine. That’s largely because her mother, Eleanor Coppola, was always by her side—lurking and observing and recording 80 hours of behind-the-scenes footage with her digital camera inside the halls of Versailles."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Eleanor shelved the footage for 14 years, then dusted it off with Sofia during the pandemic, hoping to turn her personal material into an archival documentary. Now, two years after Eleanor’s passing (and 20 since the release of Marie Antoinette ), Sofia has completed her mother’s vision, with editor Aaron Matthews compiling and editing Eleanor’s digital library—captured entirely throughout the movie’s 57-day shoot—and bringing it to vivid life. More ephemeral and narratively considered than an electronic press kit and infused with a mother’s instinctual, appreciative, encouraging eye, Making Marie Antoinette functions as both an engrossing time capsule of a young filmmaker finding her voice and a privileged peek behind the curtain of an initially misunderstood classic that now has a Criterion 4K."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Perhaps fittingly, Eleanor’s decision to hover in the margins of Marie Antoinette was not her natural setting. It had been 15 years since Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker’s Apocalypse , the acclaimed 1991 documentary she co-directed about the making of her husband’s Apocalypse Now , but this time she approached the camera with a striking degree of self-consciousness. Woven alongside highlights of her daughter’s filmmaking prowess are Eleanor’s diary entries, narrated by Diane Lane, in which she reflects on her place as a creative and questions whether she even deserves to be holding the camera. “I’m basically a shy person and I hate to intrude,” she says. “It’s counter to my personality to shoot a documentary. And yet, over and over again, I do it.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "That hesitation, and Eleanor’s awareness of her own interference, unexpectedly gives her more intimate access. She quietly courts the affections of Kirsten Dunst prepping for a scene, listens in on side conversations between producers managing logistical concerns, and finds herself close enough to capture the small, unguarded moments—like Jason Schwartzman fooling around with a harpsichord—that a more assertive, prescriptive documentarian might have missed. Much like seeing the source material behind a frequently circulated meme, it’s both illuminating and jarring seeing certain iconic behind-the-scenes stills (namely, Dunst and Schwartzman looking intently at a MacBook) recontextualized through Eleanor’s lens, invigorating them with smalltalk, laughter, and background music."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Like the best making-of movies, Making Marie Antoinette takes special aim to highlight the craftsmanship at work. There’s plenty to go around, starting with costume designer Milena Canonero, who designed 72 unique gowns for Dunst. article_text:
Note: This review was originally published as part of our 2026 NYFF coverage. The film arrives in theaters on October 23 and on MUBI on November 6.

Wrapped inside the visual splendor, luxurious elegance, and ornate decoration of Sofia Coppola’s resplendent and anachronistic Marie Antoinette is the story of a young woman leaving her family behind to help lead another country—an unknown journey and simultaneous document of wealth, excess, and its depressive isolation. Yet despite Coppola tapping into her short filmography’s recurring themes, at least on set, she never contended with the same separation and loneliness of her ill-fated heroine. That’s largely because her mother, Eleanor Coppola, was always by her side—lurking and observing and recording 80 hours of behind-the-scenes footage with her digital camera inside the halls of Versailles.

Eleanor shelved the footage for 14 years, then dusted it off with Sofia during the pandemic, hoping to turn her personal material into an archival documentary. Now, two years after Eleanor’s passing (and 20 since the release of Marie Antoinette ), Sofia has completed her mother’s vision, with editor Aaron Matthews compiling and editing Eleanor’s digital library—captured entirely throughout the movie’s 57-day shoot—and bringing it to vivid life. More ephemeral and narratively considered than an electronic press kit and infused with a mother’s instinctual, appreciative, encouraging eye, Making Marie Antoinette functions as both an engrossing time capsule of a young filmmaker finding her voice and a privileged peek behind the curtain of an initially misunderstood classic that now has a Criterion 4K.

Perhaps fittingly, Eleanor’s decision to hover in the margins of Marie Antoinette was not her natural setting. It had been 15 years since Hearts of Darkness: A Filmmaker’s Apocalypse , the acclaimed 1991 documentary she co-directed about the making of her husband’s Apocalypse Now , but this time she approached the camera with a striking degree of self-consciousness. Woven alongside highlights of her daughter’s filmmaking prowess are Eleanor’s diary entries, narrated by Diane Lane, in which she reflects on her place as a creative and questions whether she even deserves to be holding the camera. “I’m basically a shy person and I hate to intrude,” she says. “It’s counter to my personality to shoot a documentary. And yet, over and over again, I do it.”

That hesitation, and Eleanor’s awareness of her own interference, unexpectedly gives her more intimate access. She quietly courts the affections of Kirsten Dunst prepping for a scene, listens in on side conversations between producers managing logistical concerns, and finds herself close enough to capture the small, unguarded moments—like Jason Schwartzman fooling around with a harpsichord—that a more assertive, prescriptive documentarian might have missed. Much like seeing the source material behind a frequently circulated meme, it’s both illuminating and jarring seeing certain iconic behind-the-scenes stills (namely, Dunst and Schwartzman looking intently at a MacBook) recontextualized through Eleanor’s lens, invigorating them with smalltalk, laughter, and background music.

Like the best making-of movies, Making Marie Antoinette takes special aim to highlight the craftsmanship at work. There’s plenty to go around, starting with costume designer Milena Canonero, who designed 72 unique gowns for Dunst. Not to mention the herculean task of adorning every other actor and extra with their own period-specific clothing, makeup, and wigs that are cleaned and powdered every day. At one point an assistant notes that the production loses a whole day each week because of that prep time, and it becomes clear that Sofia isn’t just directing a costume drama, but orchestrating an entire ensemble of department heads and go-betweens whose execution and audibles must align in precise fashion for this operation be successful. It’s a burdensome load, but in chronicling the handmade labor, inflexible budget, and ruthless schedule needed inside a palace that never grants access to cinematic endeavors, Eleanor reminds us how much moviemaking relies on mystical qualities: cooperation and collaboration.

Still, as much as it feels like a miracle that those disparate parts come together and keep production on pace, Eleanor is also cognizant of the tenuous moments that require Sofia to raise her voice and maintain vision amidst the chaos. “It feels like I was left out of that discussion,” she tells someone who explains why extras aren’t ready for a scene. That might initially seem like a timid, albeit passive-aggressive reaction, but it’s an educational reminder of the male-dominated space Sofia constantly occupies—an ironic juxtaposition considering most of the movie is spent beside women eating fruit and chocolates in candy-coated dresses and skyscraping hairdos. Later into shooting, as though eager to show her daughter’s own growth on set, Eleanor deftly eavesdrops on another mild confrontation between Sofia and her cinematographer. This time, the director takes a firmer stance regarding the camera’s point of view sticking with her protagonist. “It’s not the guy’s story,” she says.

If those interactions capture some tension Sofia might be feeling on set, there are plenty more that reflect the beauty and levity surrounding the production every day. In many ways, Marie Antoinette was a family affair—starting with Sofia’s brother Roman, who parachutes in to film second-unit scenes and offer Sofia another set of eyes. There’s even a few days with her father, Francis, who effectively grants permission to keep fighting for her vision amidst the crowd of opinions. “Throw a Marie Antoinette party and invite everyone to it,” he advises. “Do it the way you want to.” But those bursts of help pale in comparison to Eleanor’s own omnipresence with Sofia. Near the beginning of production she observes Sofia’s worsening cold and eventually calls a doctor to diagnose her bronchitis. Later, in a scene between Marie and her mother, Eleanor deftly pans her lens to the left to capture Sofia looking through the camera, aware of the relationship parallels at play.

Careful to consider Eleanor’s feelings and reflections without ever sacrificing the pace and chronological flow of the production it’s capturing, Making Marie Antoinette saves its most insightful charms for its end. The best documentaries about the creative process inspire and breed the desire to create. It’s clear that the filmmaking process alone has reinvigorated Eleanor’s artistic inner life (even while it’s ironically made Sofia reconsider ever making such an expensive movie again). “Shouldn’t I be engaged in my own creative process, not just observing the work of my talented family?” she asks. She would answer that internal question ten years later, becoming the oldest woman to direct her feature debut with 2016’s Paris Can Wait . It’s the kind of full-circle moment that makes this documentary feel like finding a long-lost puzzle piece and snapping it into its colorful, connective place.

Making Marie Antoinette screened at the 64th New York Film Festival and will arrive in theaters on October 23 and on MUBI on November 6.

article_text:
50 Cent is having trouble logging in to our Zoom. Multiple links have been sent his way — three, by my count — to no avail. The imbroglio is excusable given the early hour and the number of different directions he’s currently being pulled, with 40 projects spread across 12 different networks, not to mention the podcasts, movies and revitalizing the city of Shreveport, Louisiana, home to his G-Unit Films and Television studio. We must chat via Zoom because 50 is back home in Houston, Texas, having decamped from his native New York City in 2021.

Related Stories

Christy Carlson Romano Says Her Salary Was Half of Shia LaBeouf's on 'Even Stevens': 'We Were Co-Leads and Had the Same Screen Time'

“I’m trying to get it together over here!” he explains upon entering the video chat. “For a second there we were experiencing technical difficulties.”

Popular on Variety

The occasion for the chat is “Street Fighter,” a new blockbuster film adaptation of the popular video game series. Directed by Kitao Sakurai (“Bad Trip”), the film centers Ryu (Andrew Koji) and his adoptive brother Ken ( Noah Centineo ), two seasoned fighters who are recruited by Chun-Li (Callina Liang) to enter a World Warrior tournament held by the dictator M. Bison (David Dastmalchian), who has designs on extracting Ryu’s fighting power for personal gain. 50 plays Balrog, a boxer who works for Bison with a distinctive hi-top fade and pointed-front hairdo. The character was modeled after Mike Tyson; and to get into fighting shape, 50 trained three hours a day for nine weeks, dropping from 238 pounds to 200 pounds. “And no, I didn’t do no weight-loss shot!” he exclaims.

These days, 50 — who is now 51 — is more business magnate than hip-hop artist, presiding over a sprawling TV empire that includes the “Power” universe and “Fightland” on Starz, and eye-opening documentaries like the Emmy-winning Netflix docuseries “Sean Combs: The Reckoning,” that exposed the evils of the artist sometimes known as Diddy . He’s also prepping a Hulu docuseries on himself .

He spoke about it all, from Trump and Diddy to the tragic loss of his mom and why he won’t work with “Power” showrunner Courtney Kemp again (along with her response), in a no-holds-barred interview with Variety .

Right? They’re not even up and functioning from last night!

Haha! I started playing with the idea of it ahead of time with my barber, and we decided there was no way to do it without cutting back into my hairline to create the outline of where [the hair piece] goes. It was tough keeping it in place once we started the fight scenes. They were doing touch-ups all the time. When I got ready to get out of there, I had no facial hair and no nothing! I was like, yo, I have to do Vegas tomorrow!

You know what’s crazy? I have to lose weight to look intensely in shape. I’ve got it, it’s just under the stuff. Some people fight their way up to gain mass, but I fight my way down. I can look like security, bro. I get big . You’re going to see me soon looking big in another action-film project that I’m going to work on.

That was the idea of the producer Cale [Boyter], who was cool. The character is based on Mike Tyson, and anybody who knows Mike knows that if it wasn’t boxing for him, it would have been armed robbery. That’s just who he was with the level of aggression that came out of Brownsville. So, my character is just coming out of jail and able to be in the tournament with the rest of them. He wants to fight everywhere .

Mike dedicated his fight [in June 2000 against Lou Savarese] to “Hommo.” But Mike wasn’t aware what happened. That’s just what they do at home. My connections to Mike are my connections to the street. I clashed with Jimmy Henchman and Mike had connections to Jimmy, too. When Mike started seeing me in places, he would look at me [knowingly] and go, “Yo,” like 50 is the real deal and the real shit right there. One time, I was going into the casino and ran into Mike and he told me, “50, I’m glad you’re with him, but he’s not going to know when to stop [spending]. He’s me.” He was talking about Floyd [Mayweather]. And you see Floyd’s financial state now, and he kind of did what Mike did with the finances.

But I love him. He’s like a brother, and we never needed each other. We are our own separate entities that have established ourselves in different ways. There were benefits to me being around at the time, since he didn’t have the social following that he has now. He would say, “Tell 5 to post this and it’s going to be all over the place!” He was sending me the blurb of what he wanted out there, so I’d post it and then it’d be all over the place. But we connected even prior to my success in music. He flew his entire entourage to Puerto Rico to see me in 2002, even before “Get Rich or Die Tryin.’” He knew I was going to be the biggest thing in music.

I did. I think I live vicariously through [Mayweather] in the sense of not just being a fighter but being the best fighter. Boxing isn’t a sport you can play. You can play basketball, football and baseball, but in boxing, if you’re losing and getting your ass whooped, you’re just not good enough and not on the level. Each time you get out of the ring punch-drunk you have a personal epiphany about what you’re doing! You think, “Fuck it, I could do construction. I don’t need to be doing this shit.”

Yeah! I worked for 30 days with the boxing trainer they had in Australia even before we started working with the stunt crew, so the moves were programmed in my system. We rehearsed it at half-speed and then bop-bop ! I think it’s because he was doing so many stunts in the movie, so he didn’t slip and the punch just got him. I was like, “My bad, bro! You didn’t move!” He was like, “Oh, shit. All right. Come on, it’s OK.” And we just went right back into doing it. But that was a crazy moment, and I felt bad because it’s rare that I actually like everyone involved in a project, but I had fun with these people and I’d go back and do it again in a heartbeat. Cody [Rhodes] got a yacht for the whole cast for one weekend while we were in Australia and I rented out an amusement park and took the entire cast and crew as well as their loved ones.

Courtney [Kemp]. I don’t look forward to working with her ever again. I don’t think that she’s wholeheartedly a bad person, I just think that it got out of control for her. After the success of “Power,” she would go, “I wrote it.” Well, you did write it, but I uploaded everything that you wrote, and we got a “no” from everybody before we got a “yes,” and I wrote songs that captured, at its nucleus, each one of the leads that we had and that emotionally captured energy for scenes. When we went to pitch “Power” to Chris Albrecht [then-CEO of Starz], we’d pitch the show and then we would play a minute and 30 seconds of a song, and then we’d pitch the show and play another minute and 30 seconds of a song. I produced eight songs that went into it, including the theme song.

I think she forgot. Because in the beginning, the sell for the show was “50 Cent.” That’s it. There was a point with Albrecht where I was like, “Y’all know what time it is, and I’ll tell you when the show comes back on.” And then Starz watched 40% of their subscribers disappear. They called me in to the office to talk about it, and said, “What kind of partner does this?!” I said, “You guys have been doing this a lot longer than I have, and I want to be clear that if you’re not identifying that you have a programming issue, then I don’t know what to say to you. Me saying, ‘Y’all know what time it is, and I’ll tell you when the show comes back on” means that you have nothing else on this network that people want to watch. They’ll cancel the subscription and then come back when it’s back on.” So, then I pitched them the “Power” universe. They didn’t want the “Power” universe; I forced the “Power” universe on them when they saw the forty percent decrease. It opened the idea up to them of, “Oh, let’s put some more of it on so we can force the subscribers to stay.” And it put me in a different position where they were like, “Oh… He can fuck us up and turn this shit off.”

It made them see things a little bit differently. Chris [Albrecht] is such an innovative thinker that he saw the opportunity to make it great. And the budgeting for the original “Power” had gotten so fuckin’ high that the show cost nearly $12 million an episode. All the clothes you saw weren’t being sent. Every single clothing item on the show was being purchased three times. I was like, “What the fuck are you doing that for? They need to promote the clothing company.”

When it came time to do “BMF” and the different shows, I lowered the budget because I had the clothing companies giving us clothes for promotional purposes, since they’ll get ten million eyeballs on it. There was all kinds of weird shit going on, but it got to a point where Courtney was trying to run the entire network through one show. She also said she didn’t want to do “Raising Kanan” because she didn’t want to tell a story where they already know the ending. Half the shit she was saying just didn’t make sense. I told her, “This is the late-‘80s going into the ‘90s, and that was the golden era for the drug trade.” Sascha [Penn] was able to make a masterpiece out of it that ran for five seasons.

(In a statement to Variety , Kemp responded: “While 50’s recollection of budgets and production requirements is uninformed, as he was rarely in a budget meeting, I have never once understated his importance in the genesis of ‘Power.’ While he did not write nor create the series, he was a large part of its birth. That said, I am completely bewildered by his need to mention me in interviews or podcasts. I have completely moved on in my career, and I hope that the imminent success of ‘Street Fighter’ allows him to do the same.”)

I wasn’t surprised. When it came to the Diddy doc, I had started it six months before I was able to get Alex Stapleton, the showrunner. And it’s important to understand that she is the reason why it’s great. It could have been over-aggressive where it felt like you’re attacking the person, but she used people’s perspectives to tell their truth. And what he did was actually worse than what’s in the doc.

When you look at the Cassie situation, people think of just the hallway [attack]. But you have to look at what transpired that made it get to that point where you’re kicking her on the floor, and where it didn’t even matter to him what he did to her. He also got in the habit of not paying people — even his artists, where he raked them and took their publishing — and he used that as a form of control.

And what was that for? That was for his dealings with Cassie. [Diddy] had the habit of dealing with someone else’s woman. Like, every woman you’ve seen him with was with someone from celebrity culture prior to him, including Cassie who was with Ryan Leslie. He kind of took her from Ryan Leslie. And his choices are not by chance. He picks the person based on who they were with prior. He needed confirmation of his success through who they were with prior to him.

Haha! I know Rob. They sent a bouquet of flowers over and I thought, “OK, I know where that came from.”

It didn’t have anything crazy on the note, but it was definitely for me.

There were things that didn’t surface publicly that were attempts from him to damage the perception of me. He had people saying things about his activities that went back years and years, and these things didn’t surface until they removed the statute of limitations from sexual-assault allegations. Recently, he had a law firm that pulled away from him after [his accusers] had the ability to move forward with a lawsuit against him, which is weird because usually law firms will take their 30% contingency in the case. That same law firm has sixty sexual-assault cases for him. And it’s been two years already. Imagine responding to each of those lawsuits? That’s probably $150,000 a piece, or $9 million total. So, when he saw the $9 million bill, he probably went, “I didn’t agree to that bill!” The law firm is probably going to end up suing him.

He was trying to find people to make frivolous accusations against me. From his perspective, it was, “How do I cloud what’s going to happen to me?” You hear him on the phone in the doc saying he needed people in the media to help him discredit everybody else.

It does feel like that because it was the best presentation of it. But look, it wasn’t top secret, bro. He was saying that stuff in books. That information was clear and out there. The problem with getting away with things is that the person feels they can get away with anything , so then they regress further and do something later that turns into their downfall. It’s rare that people get away with things and then decide not to do those things again. It makes you feel like you have the power to get away with shit, so you do more shit like try to blow up Kid Cudi’s car. And where’s the police report for the car blowing up? Where are the police reports for people getting shot in the studio?

Now, Netflix has such a wide reach that this went global. And international folks feel that if 50 is saying it, this is going to be the real hip hop insider shit that goes on. You know how important real is to hip hop and youth culture. These kids now will tell you who they shot last week and create a visual picture of the crime scene.

Yeah. A few guys out there wrote shit that was so accurate, I was like, “Damn! You just told on yourself! What the fuck is that?!” I was writing about stories I’d experienced, but those were situations in the past.

The tickets were going for that cheap on Groupon! I said, “I want those first three rows.” I know what it feels like when they put the crowd too far back, so since it’s all digital, I saw that I got all the tickets but maybe four in the first three rows.

Probably a small portion of it. There will be certain things that we talk about. It’s really less important to my life than people see it. In the docuseries, you’ll see me get emotional at points, but usually about what happened before. The loss of my mom — that is where I was the most confused and vulnerable.

Yeah. So, you’ve got to imagine when you only really have her — since I didn’t know my dad at all — when they tried to explain to me, “Your mom is gone, and she’s not coming back,” I was like, “No, she’s going to come back.” I couldn’t even process it at that point. And then I stayed at my grandmother’s. All that was rough, so we’ll reflect back on that and also talk about other stuff. When I got shot is not the first time I’d been shot at, or me shooting at other people.

Marlow, look: When your mom has friends around, you look at them and just see friends. And how often does a woman have a female friend that she’s close to that she talks with often? As a child, I just saw two women hanging out. My grandmother informed me later that there was more going on and they weren’t just friends, and I was like, “Oh! Now I know what that was!” I’m not ashamed of that in any way. I grew up around that. I used vulnerability at the time I explained it, going, “Coming up I was confused, my mommy kissing a girl / Confusion occurs comin’ up in the cold world.”

Yeah. Other people have those things in their experience and their upbringing, but they leave it out because they don’t think that’s “cool.” I didn’t care about being vulnerable — it made it more powerful for me because I know someone else has had that experience and would understand it.

No, but it is something we have in common.

But then, find the line. We just reacted differently to it. One of us doesn’t mind, and the other one kind of minds a little bit.

I have 40 shows across 12 different networks, and 10 are going toward air. I completed 18 episodes of “Power: Origins” that are coming and also released “Fightland,” which was my first international show since it was U.K.-based, and am preparing for the second season of it. We still didn’t get the nod yet, but I think the success of the project commands that. I’ve seen the numbers. There’s my own doc at Hulu that we’re working on and a heap of other projects. There’s “Cash Kings,” which two networks want, and then “Bone Parish” at Starz, along with “Billion Dollar Lawyer” and “Power: Legacy.”

Haha. And then Peacock has an adaptation of my book “The Accomplice,” which will star Taraji P. Henson. I got the dream cast and crew that I wanted for that one.

People make interesting choices, and sometimes you don’t know why they’re doing it. I think it’s a lack of a clear understanding of everything that’s going on. I try to stay as purple as possible, you know what I’m saying? I don’t understand things that are going on from the Democratic side at points, and then I don’t understand some of the mentality that’s connected to the Republican side. I think when people get ready to actually vote, they do it based on what’s affecting them. But I don’t have beef with nobody, especially in that realm. When you start to do big business, it becomes political because you see the state or local government provide aid for it since it will employ a lot of people. What can start out as a project for the studios can become a whole revitalization of a city.

Yeah. It becomes a way bigger deal because my instincts are to just go for it. I’ve already accomplished so much given where I’ve come from, so just try your luck convincing me that I can’t do it, bro. I’m already convinced I can.

article_text:
Jakarta Governor Pramono Anung Wibowo kicked off the Jakarta Film Summit 2026 on Tuesday with a pitch for the Indonesian capital as a regional film hub, making the case that the city is equipped to draw more shoots, filmmakers and investors from across the region.

Speaking at the Royal Glass House at Park Hyatt Jakarta, Pramono built his argument around the city’s infrastructure, its economy and its transit system. He held up Busan, the South Korean port city that is home to the Busan International Film Festival , as an example Jakarta could learn from as it grows its own industry.

Related Stories

‘You Can See Everything’ Sets Oscar Campaigns for Best Picture, Supporting Actress and More Categories

The governor cited economic growth of 5.52% and inflation of 2.7%. Jakarta has climbed from 17th to 15th place in a global transport ranking, according to the figures he presented, and public transit now connects 93% of the city.

The summit, hosted by the Jakarta Film Commission with the Indonesian Film Agency (Badan Perfilman Indonesia, or BPI), runs through Oct. 22, with the first two days given over to production policy, filming permits, incentives, financing and investment. Upward of 500 attendees from 10 countries are taking part, with 40 speakers on the bill. Government officials and financial institutions are in the room alongside investors, streamers and industry professionals.

Tuesday’s sessions dealt with how government can back productions, including opening up shooting locations around Jakarta. An ASEAN Film Alliance Network panel examined how to nurture talent, raise money and set up co-productions across the region.

The focus will shift to money on Oct. 21. Panels will cover how to get a project ready for funding, what role banks can play, and how audience data can help investors gauge risk.

The final day, Jakarta Scouting Day, will take film commissioners and production companies out to prospective locations including Pasar Rumput, Muara Angke Harbor, Kota Tua and the Bundaran HI Skydeck. Also on the schedule is “The Two Cities,” which will pair Jakarta with Hong Kong to explore ways the two might work together.

Organizers hope the event will yield policy recommendations, build up industry capacity and lift Jakarta’s international standing as a filming destination.

Fauzan Zidni, chair of BPI, said: “Jakarta Film Summit shows that local government can be a strategic partner for the film industry. When policy, permits, and financing are discussed at the same table with filmmakers, we are no longer working in silos. BPI is ready to make sure the recommendations from this forum are translated into policies that filmmakers can feel on the ground.”

article_text:
More than a decade after the Sony hack shook Hollywood, Martin Scorsese is still reeling from the fallout of the North Korean state-sponsored digital attack.

The Oscar-winning director recalled how the wide-reaching hack, which was a response to Seth Rogen ‘s 2014 film The Interview , “ruined everything” for Scorsese’s planned Cleopatra feature, which would have starred Angelina Jolie.

“Remember we were gonna do Cleopatra at one point, and then they made fun of [ Kim Jong Un ], and he got mad and he blew up everybody at Columbia,” he told daughter Francesca Scorsese on Tribeca’s Crafty . “Seth Rogen, right? And then he got mad, and [it] ruined Cleopatra .”

Related Stories

Martin Scorsese Joins Bahman Ghobadi’s Eva Green Horror Film ‘Trees Are Watching’ Ahead Of Toronto Bow

‘The Studio’s Seth Rogen And Co-Creator Evan Goldberg On The “Miracle” Of Casting Scorsese And What Ron Howard Said About His Role

Martin added, “We were gonna do it. We were ready on the script. Angelina Jolie—We were going. She was gonna be Cleopatra VII. It was gonna be really wild.”

Watch on Deadline

As Francesca told her father she’s “so mad about” the fate of the film, Martin quipped, “Well, tell Seth, because they ruined everything. Just because Kim Jong Un doesn’t have a sense of humor.”

In The Interview , co-written and directed by Rogen and Evan Goldberg, celebrity tabloid show host Dave Skylark (James Franco) and his producer Aaron Rapaport (Rogen) land a rare interview with Kim Jong Un (Randall Park). When the CIA catches wind, they enlist the pair to assassinated the North Korean dictator.

Despite the unintended consequences of The Interview , Scorsese and Rogen have moved on, as the former even played himself in last year’s debut episode of the latter’s Apple TV series The Studio . Since Rogen’s studio head character Matt Remick ends up responsible for Scorsese’s passion project getting axed, could the storyline be another meta example of life imitating art in the smash show?

article_text:
11月9日（月）まで奈良国立博物館で開催中の第78回正倉院展。多彩なオリジナルグッズも注目です。今回は、第78回正倉院展のグッズとして、一澤信三郎帆布によるコラボバッグを紹介します。（美術展ナビ関西）

◇New!! 追加情報 【受注販売】一澤信三郎帆布×正倉院展 トートバッグ（2027年1月中旬以降順次発送予定） ※本商品は 現地特設ショップ「天平」では完売しました。 10月29日 (木) 正午から「美術展ナビオンラインストア」で注文受付開始予定です。

◇正倉院展のチケットは美術展ナビチケットアプリで発売中

正倉院の美と京の手仕事

一澤信三郎帆布によるコラボバッグは、聖武天皇ゆかりの宝物のひとつ「 紺牙撥鏤碁子 」（第78回正倉院展に出陳されます​）をモチーフとしています。碁石の両面には、「 花喰鳥 」と呼ばれる、くちばしに花枝をくわえたカモがあらわされています。

幸福を運ぶとされる「花喰鳥」は、おめでたい吉祥文様。深い紺色の帆布は紺牙撥鏤碁子の地色を思わせ、白と朱で表現された鳥文様はまるで、小さな碁子がそのままバッグになったようです。1300年の時を超えて受け継がれた美意識を、毎日の装いの中で楽しんでいただける特別な一品です。

職人が一つ一つ丁寧に

このバッグを手がけた一澤信三郎帆布は、1905年創業の京都・東山の帆布かばん店です。創業以来、職人たちの道具袋づくりから始まり、現在も京都で製造・販売を続けています。 一澤信三郎帆布のかばんづくりには、一貫した哲学があります。 「丈夫で長持ち、シンプルで使いやすく、飽きのこないかばん」。 素材選びから裁断、縫製、修理までを京都で行う「製造直売」の形を守り続けており、職人が一つ一つ丁寧に仕立てています。

工房では、まず帆布を裁断し、職人が木槌を使って生地に折り目をつけながら形を整えます。その後、長年使い込まれた工業用ミシンで丁寧に縫製。ミシンをかける職人と、帆布に印をつけたり金具を取り付けたりする下職が二人一組とチームとなって最後の仕上げまで一貫して製造を担います。手間ひまをかけ、丈夫で長持ちするかばんを作り続けています。

使い込むほど「ええ味」

使い込むほどに風合いを増し、長く愛用できることも大きな魅力。使い込むことで帆布は少しずつ柔らかくなり、持ち主の暮らしに寄り添うように形を変えていきます。 修理をしながら長く使う愛用者も多く、使い込まれたかばんの修理依頼が数多く寄せられています。長年の使用によって生まれる風合いを「ええ味」と呼び、その変化も魅力のひとつとして受け継がれています。 1300年前の天平の美と、120年を超えて受け継がれる京都の職人技。正倉院展だからこそ実現した特別な一品です。

◇【受注販売】一澤信三郎帆布×正倉院展 トートバッグ（2027年1月中旬以降順次発送予定） ※本商品は 現地特設ショップ「天平」では完売しました。 10月29日 (木) 正午から「美術展ナビオンラインストア」で注文受付開始予定です。

紺牙撥鏤碁子トートバッグ

製作：一澤信三郎帆布

素材：綿帆布

価格：15,950円

販売場所：現地特設ショップ「天平」では完売しました。 10月29日 (木) 正午から「美術展ナビオンラインストア」で注文受付開始予定です。 ※一澤信三郎帆布の店舗での販売はありません

第78回 正倉院展

会場：奈良国立博物館 東西新館（奈良市登大路町50 奈良公園内）

会期：2026年10月24日（土）～11月9日（月）

休館日：会期中は無休

開場時間：8:00～18:00 ※金土日祝は20時まで （入場は閉館の60分前まで）

観覧料（日時指定券）：一般2,000円（1,500円）、高大生1,500円（1,000円）、小中生500円（無料）、キャンパスメンバーズ学生400円 ※カッコ内はレイト割料金（月～木は16時以降、金～日と祝日は17時以降） 日時指定枠に空きがある場合には、博物館敷地内の特設窓口にて当日の「日時指定券」を販売するが、1枚ごとに200円の発券料がかかる。

詳しくは 博物館公式ホームページ へ。

◇【記者会見】「第78回正倉院展」奈良国立博物館で10月24日から11月9日まで開催 足利将軍が蘭奢待を切った日に見た龍のミイラも 実用性や機能美など奈良時代のモノづくりに注目

◇【第78回正倉院展】チケットは9月4日販売開始 お得なレイト割を設定 レクチャー付きや手ぬぐい付きチケットも オリジナルグッズ、公開講座情報なども発表 奈良国立博物館東西新館で10月24日から11月9日まで

◇第78回正倉院展の多彩なオリジナルグッズが発表 奈良国立博物館で10月24日から11月9日まで

◇正倉院ゆかりの講師による特別講演会付き「正倉院展」鑑賞ツアー 10月30日、11月2日、11月4日に開催 参加者募集中 tabiwaトラベル

article_text:
Films and events

Laugh

Too Many Beasts

L’Espece explosive

In this deliciously unhinged mash-up of rural thriller and dark comedy, enormous wild boars create havoc in a small French town.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Sarah Arnold

Screenwriters Sarah Arnold, Jérémie Dubois, Olivier Seror, Romain Winkler, Mehdi Ben Attia

With Alexis Manenti, Ella Rumpf, Vincent Dedienne

France 2026. 95min

Courtesy of Playtime

Language French With English subtitles

Introduction

Farmers and hunters are openly at war in the rural town of Sérieux. Wild boars are ruining crops and putting everyone on edge. When a local farmer mysteriously disappears, gendarme Fulda is put on the case. As he reluctantly teams up with psychologist Stéphane, the investigation gradually spirals out of control, and so does this offbeat and absurdly funny comedy.

Laure Bonville

With thanks to Unifrance.

Content advice

Contains scenes of animal slaughter, drug use, and nudity.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Wild Horse Nine

Martin McDonagh continues to mine the absurdities and complexities of male relationships in a film that brims with energy and is sure to delight.

The History of Concrete

Having attended a Hallmark movie workshop, John Wilson applies his learnings to a documentary about concrete, albeit with a dryly funny and deceptively understated tone.

The Fox

A talking fox, voiced by Olivia Colman, persuades a hunter to transform his cheating wife into an ideal spouse, in this gleefully outrageous, shape-shifting comedy.

title_original: India’s Yellowstone International Film Festival Announces Documentary And LGBTQIA+ Slates
editorial_title_zh: 印度的黄石国际电影节公布纪录片与 LGBTQIA+ 展映片单
editorial_excerpt_zh: 独家：印度孟买即将举办的黄石国际电影节公布了其纪录片展映片单，其中的亮点是奥斯卡竞争者《美国医生》的亚洲首映。导演波·西·滕（Poh Si Teng）的这部电影审视了三位志愿提供医疗……

"由顾万成（Wancheng Gu）和普拉萨德·谢蒂（Prasad Shetty）联合执导的纪录片长片《狼》（The Wolf）“讲述了上海一位60岁的酷儿前村长袁（Yuan）的故事，她在晚年寻求自主与重塑自我时，在爱情、家庭责任和不断变化的经济格局中穿行。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "在 Deadline 上观看", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黄石国际电影节将于11月30日至12月4日在印度马哈拉施特拉邦首府孟买举行。电影节展映的短片纪录片之一是莱利·菲奇帕特里克（Riley Fitchpatrick）执导的《诞生的秘密》（Born Secret），片中这位电影制作人“回到了建造了原子弹的家乡。”滑动查看片单中的纪录片短片。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Elephants-in-the-Fog.png?w=247", "alt": "‘Elephants in the Fog’", "caption": "YIFF", "credit": "Deadline · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "YIFF 还公布了其 LGBTQIA+ 主题电影片单。除纪录片《狼》外，剧情长片还包括获得2026年戛纳电影节一种关注单元评审团奖的《雾中大象》（Elephants in the Fog）。该片由阿比纳什·比克拉姆·沙（Abinash Bikram Shah）执导，“讲述了尼泊尔村庄里 Kinnar（跨性别）社区的女家长皮拉蒂（Pirati）的故事，她梦想着逃离并过上普通的生活。当她的一个女儿失踪时，她必须展开调查并在爱与责任之间做出选择。”", "links": [{"text": "YIFF", "url": "https://deadline.com/tag/yiff/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "《坦克时间》（Tank Time）（LGBTQIA+ 短片）—— 一个孤独的非二元性别青少年在一只被偷的鱼、一场邻里间的微小宿怨以及一次意料之外的心动中找到了勇气、友谊和一丝魔力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影人 – 杰斯·伯吉斯（Jess Burgess）；国家 – 美国；时长 -16:39", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "《维哈尔湖的女巫》（The Witch of Vihar Lake）（LGBTQIA+ 短片）米图（Mitthu）是一个胆小的小男孩，他和十几岁的姐姐伊希塔（Ishita）住在维哈尔湖附近的一个村庄里，那里流传着关于一个可怕女巫的故事。当地村民不敢靠近森林或那个闹鬼的湖泊。当这对姐弟与父母的无知和愤怒作斗争时，神秘与魔法环绕着他们。随着女巫的威胁笼罩着他们的生活，我们跟随中了魔法的伊希塔和米图开启他们的成长的旅程。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影人 – 乔伊·考希克（Joey Kaushik）；国家 – 印度；时长 – 10:47", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "《水手与厨师》（The Sailor & The Chef）——（LGBTQIA+ 纪录短片）皮尤什（Piyush）和苏希尔（Sushil）30年前在印度孟买的一家剧院里完全偶然地相遇了。当时他们彼此并不知情，两人都是同性恋，并在互联网刚刚兴起、几乎没有什么公开且引以为傲的酷儿社区的时代寻找伴侣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影人 - 阿希什·索尼（Ashish Sawhny）；国家 – 印度；时长 -20:23", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在今年的电影节上，YIFF 联合凯沙夫·苏里基金会（KSF）和莲花视觉制作公司（Lotus Visual Productions）推出了首届 KSF 酷儿资助计划，承诺提供20,000美元“用于支持印度新兴 LGBTQIA+ 电影人的独立电影制作。该倡议将挑选两名电影人，每人获得10,000美元的制作资金，并享有为期九个月的行业导师指导以及全方位的创意和制作支持。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "YIFF 指出，该资助计划已确立了三年的承诺，以确保该倡议的长期可持续性和影响力。“在这三年期间，合作组织旨在支持六位电影人制作六部电影，为新兴的酷儿叙事者提供资源和机会，将他们的故事带进现实并与世界分享。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Tushar-Tyagi-YIFF-Director-2026.jpeg?w=200", "alt": "图沙尔·蒂亚吉（Tushar Tyagi），黄石国际电影节创始人", "caption": "图沙尔·蒂亚吉（Tushar Tyagi），黄石国际电影节 YIFF 创始人", "credit": "Deadline · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "黄石国际电影节创始人图沙尔·蒂亚吉（Tushar Tyagi）表示：“人才和引人入胜的故事随处可见，但将它们搬上银幕的机会并不总是对所有人开放。对于印度的许多酷儿电影人而言，挑战并非缺乏想象力或可讲的故事，而是缺乏将创意愿景转化为电影所需的资源、行业网络和支持。通过这项资助，我们希望提供自由和资金，让电影人能够以诚实和真实的方式讲述他们的故事，从而帮助弥合这一鸿沟。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "蒂亚吉接着说道：“我们的雄心是培育新一代的印度酷儿之声，将根植于真实生活经验的叙事搬上银幕，并为这些故事走出国门创造机会。这些故事不仅值得被讲述，更值得被全世界的观众看到、听到和颂扬。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Keshav-Suri.jpg?w=300", "alt": "凯沙夫·苏里基金会创始人凯沙夫·苏里（Keshav Suri）", "caption": "凯沙夫·苏里基金会（Keshav Suri Foundation）创始人凯沙夫·苏里（Keshav Suri），YIFF", "credit": "Deadline · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "凯沙夫·苏里基金会创始人凯沙夫·苏里评论道：“电影中的代表性绝不能仅仅停留在银幕上有 LGBTQIA+ 角色。同样重要的是，来自该社群的人们必须拥有资源和创作自由来讲述他们自己的故事。社群内部绝不缺乏人才或引人入胜的故事，但获得资金和行业机会依然是一个挑战。通过这项资助，我们希望帮助弥合这一鸿沟，让更多酷儿电影人有机会将他们的故事搬上银幕。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Neeraj-Churi.png?w=300", "alt": "莲花视觉制作公司创始人尼拉吉·丘里（Neeraj Churi）", "caption": "莲花视觉制作公司（Lotus Visual Productions）创始人尼拉吉·丘里（Neeraj Churi），YIFF", "credit": "Deadline · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "莲花视觉制作公司创始人、《仙人掌梨》（Cactus Pears）圣丹斯获奖制片人尼拉吉·丘里表示：“长期以来，印度的酷儿电影人在争取资金和寻找合适的合作伙伴以实现其创意愿景方面一直面临挑战。然而，印度电影中最令人兴奋、最具原创性的声音正不断从 LGBTQIA+ 社群内部涌现。我们坚信，这些电影人理应有机会按照自己的条件讲述自己的故事。KSF 酷儿资助项目旨在创造这样的机会，将资金支持与导师指导及切实的电影制作指导结合起来。我们希望这一 initiative 不仅能促成两部电影的诞生，还能为新一代酷儿叙事者敞开大门。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "除了上文提到的《水手与大厨》（The Sailor & The Chef）和《生而为密》（Born Secret）之外，以下是入选第7届黄石国际电影节展映的短片纪录片：", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "《在寂静之后》（In the Silence After）——（纪录短片）一个儿子回到家中照顾母亲，记录下他们共同度过的最后一年。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影人 – 塞巴斯蒂安·德拉斯卡萨斯（Sebastian Delascasas）；国家 – 哥伦比亚、美国；片长 – 16:50", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "《不管天气如何》（No Matter the Weather）——（纪录短片）83岁的雷妮（Renée）摔断了脚踝。幸运的是，她可以依靠她的孙女弗洛伦斯（Florence），后者挺身而出担任她的照顾者。虽然这场磨难让她们比以往任何时候都更加亲密，但也不可避免地让她们直面雷妮身体衰退的现实。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影人 – 弗洛伦斯·拉丰（Florence Lafond）；国家 – 加拿大；片长 – 14:30", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "《德里的向日葵》（A Sunflower in Delhi）——（纪录短片）在一个仅限女性的微型美容院里，几代忠实顾客（包括电影人的家人）聚在一起，回顾着任由头发变白的过程。影片在向日葵中国美容院（Sunflower Chinese Beauty Parlour）这一私密绿洲与外面熙熙攘攘的城市景观之间辗转流连。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影人 – 雷万蒂卡·古普塔（Revantika Gupta）；国家 – 印度；片长 – 23:00", "translated": true}]

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: The upcoming Yellowstone International Film Festival in Mumbai, India has announced its documentary lineup, highlighted by the Asian premiere of Oscar contender American Doctor .

Director Poh Si Teng’s film examines three U.S. physicians who volunteered their medical expertise to treat Palestinian children severely injured in Israel’s sustained attack on Gaza (it screens Thursday at DOC NYC after being named to that festival’s prestigious shortlist).

Joining American Doctor at the Yellowstone festival will be fellow documentary feature Herland , directed by Kallol Mukherjee, also making its Asian premiere. “In a deeply conservative Indian village where women are forbidden from stepping outside without male permission, Bhagyashree and her growing sisterhood rise in defiance, claiming their right to work and confronting generations of patriarchal control,” reads a description. “As their resistance gathers force, the cost of being seen as equal begins to turn dangerous. How much are they willing to risk?”

Related Stories

Watermelon Pictures Co-Founders Talk Future Plans & Growing Hollywood Support For Palestinian Stories: "We've Been Seeing A Renaissance With A Lot Of The A-Listers"

Inaugural West Hollywood Human Rights Film Festival To Showcase Oscar-Contending Documentaries, 20th Anniversary Screening Of 'Blood Diamond'

Documentary feature The Wolf , directed by Wancheng Gu and Prasad Shetty, “follows Yuan, a 60-year-old queer former village mayor in Shanghai, as she navigates love, family obligations, and shifting economic landscapes while seeking autonomy and reinvention later in life.”

Watch on Deadline

The Yellowstone International Film Festival runs from November 30 to December 4 in Mumbai, capital of the Indian state of Maharashtra. Among the short documentaries programmed in the festival is Born Secret , directed by Riley Fitchpatrick, in which the filmmaker “returns to his hometown that built the atomic bomb . ” Scroll for the list of doc shorts in the lineup.

YIFF also revealed its slate of LGBTQIA+-themed films. In addition to documentary The Wolf , features include Elephants in the Fog , winner of the Jury Prize in the Un Certain Regard section of the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. The film directed by Abinash Bikram Shah “follows Pirati, matriarch of a Kinnar (Trans) community in a Nepalese village, who dreams of escaping to a normal life. When one of her daughters disappears, she must investigate and choose between love and responsibility.”

Tank Time (LGBTQIA Short) – A lonely, nonbinary teen finds courage, friendship, and a glimmer of magic in a stolen fish, a petty neighborhood feud, and an unexpected crush.

Filmmaker – Jess Burgess; Country – United States; Runtime -16:39

The Witch of Vihar Lake (LGBTQIA Short) Mitthu, a timid young boy and his teenage sister Ishita live in a village close to Vihar Lake, where stories of a terrifying witch prevail. The village locals don’t dare go close to the forest or the haunted lake. Mystery and magic surround the siblings as they grapple with their parents’ ignorance and anger. We follow a bewitched Ishita and Mitthu in their coming-of-age journey as the threat of the witch looms over their lives.

Filmmaker – Joey Kaushik; Country – India; Runtime – 10:47

The Sailor & The Chef – ( LGBTQIA+ Doc Short) Piyush & Sushil met entirely by chance 30 years ago at a theatre in Mumbai, India. Unbeknownst to each other, they were both gay & seeking partners in a time when the internet was nascent, and there was barely any out & proud queer community.

Filmmaker- Ashish Sawhny; Country – India; Runtime -20:23

At this year’s festival, YIFF launches the inaugural KSF Queer Grant, in association with the Keshav Suri Foundation (KSF) and Lotus Visual Productions, committing $20,000 USD “towards the production of independent films by emerging LGBTQIA+ filmmakers in India. The initiative will select two filmmakers, each receiving $10,000 USD in production funding, alongside a nine-month program of industry mentorship and end-to-end creative and production support.”

The grant has been established with a three-year commitment to ensure the long-term sustainability and impact of the initiative, YIFF notes. “Over the course of these three years, the collaborating organizations aim to support six filmmakers in producing six films, providing emerging queer storytellers with the resources and opportunities to bring their stories to life and share them with the world.”

Yellowstone International Film Festival founder Tushar Tyagi said, “Talent and compelling stories exist everywhere, but the opportunity to bring them to life is not always accessible to everyone. For many queer filmmakers in India, the challenge is not a lack of imagination or stories to tell, but access to the resources, industry networks and support needed to turn their creative vision into a film. Through this grant, we want to help bridge that gap by giving filmmakers the freedom and means to tell their stories with honesty and authenticity.”

Tyagi continued, “Our ambition is to nurture a new generation of queer Indian voices, bring narratives rooted in lived experiences to the screen, and create opportunities for these stories to travel beyond borders. These stories deserve not only to be told, but to be seen, heard and celebrated by audiences around the world.”

Keshav Suri, founder of the Keshav Suri Foundation, commented, “Representation in cinema must go beyond having LGBTQIA+ characters on screen. It is equally important that people from the community have the resources and creative freedom to tell their own stories. There is no shortage of talent or compelling stories within the community, but access to funding and industry opportunities remains a challenge. Through this grant, we want to help bridge that gap and give more queer filmmakers the opportunity to bring their stories to life.”

“For too long, queer filmmakers in India have faced challenges in securing funding and finding the right partners to bring their creative visions to life,” said Neeraj Churi, founder of Lotus Visual Productions and Sundance-winning producer of Cactus Pears . “And yet, some of the most exciting and original voices in Indian cinema are emerging from within the LGBTQIA+ community. We believe these filmmakers should have the opportunity to tell their own stories, on their own terms. The KSF Queer Grant is about creating that opportunity, combining financial support with mentorship and practical filmmaking guidance. Our hope is that this initiative will not only help make two films possible, but also open doors for a new generation of queer storytellers.”

In addition to The Sailor & The Chef and Born Secret noted above, these are the short documentaries programmed in the 7 th edition of the Yellowstone International Film Festival:

In the Silence After – (Doc Short) A son returns home to care for his mother, filming the last year they will spend together.

Filmmaker – Sebastian Delascasas; Country – Colombia, United States; Runtime -16:50

No Matter the Weather – (Doc Short) Renée, 83, broke her ankle. Fortunately, she can rely on her granddaughter Florence, who steps in as her caregiver. While this ordeal brings them closer than ever, it inevitably confronts them with the reality of Renée’s decline.

Filmmaker – Florence Lafond; Country – Canada; Runtime -14:30

A Sunflower in Delhi – (Doc Short) In a tiny women’s only beauty parlour, generations of devoted customers, including the filmmaker’s family, reflect on letting their hair go grey. The film meanders between the intimate oasis of the Sunflower Chinese Beauty Parlour and the bustling city landscape outside.

Filmmaker – Revantika Gupta; Country – India; Runtime -23:00

article_text:
Aseel AlYaqoub has been awarded the seventh Ithra Art Prize for Flora Incognita (2026), a speculative herbarium of hybrid plant forms that explores how botanical records have shaped perceptions of the Gulf. The King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture (Ithra) announced the winning project during a ceremony in Dhahran, where the prize was presented as part of the institution’s ongoing support for contemporary artistic practices in the region.

As part of the Ithra Art Prize, AlYaqoub received a USD 100,000 grant, with Flora Incognita also joining Ithra’s permanent collection. The work is currently on view at the Ithra Museum as part of an exhibition bringing together the five shortlisted projects . These include AlYaqoub’s Flora Incognita alongside Bady Dalloul’s miniature Matchboxes Drawings (2026), which examines imagery and collective memory; Heba Y Amin Elmahamly’s reworking of the historical Mahmal procession in The Last Carrier: Iteration I (2026); Ala Younis ’ Lifted Arches (2026), which brings Islamic architectural traditions into dialogue with modernism; and Jawad Al Malhi’s Ashes of Absence (2026) , which addresses disappearance and loss through a multimedia presentation.

The winning project was selected by a five-member international jury, including Farah Abushullaih , Tarek Abou El Fetouh, Dr Nada Shabout, Jérôme Sans and Nadia Kaabi-Linke .

Farah Abushullaih, the programmes manager at Ithra, noted:⁠‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​⁠ “The prize serves as a vital platform, bringing innovative ideas and artistic visions into dialogue and shaping the future of contemporary art in the region.⁠‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​⁠ By celebrating Aseel AlYaqoub, we are investing in a vision that disrupts conventional narratives and elevates the Saudi cultural landscape to new intellectual heights.”

The seventh edition also builds on the programme’s scope by supporting each of the five finalists with production funds, allowing them to create new projects responding to the region’s shifting histories and realities.

article_text:
Films and events

Official Competition

Imperium

Master of archival film reconstruction, Sergei Loznitsa, reframes Soviet history once again via the revealing gaze of Italian cameramen who captured life there in the early 1970s.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Sergei Loznitsa

Germany-France-Italy-Lithuania 2026. 176min

Courtesy of Coproduction Office

Introduction

The footage Loznitsa uncovered at Rome’s Audiovisual Archive of the Labour and Democratic Movement left him marvelling at the contrast with official Soviet productions from the same era. Opening in Moscow, the film shifts into territories where different traits, beliefs and ethnographic features emerge, revealing the powerful grip of an empire over its people. The result is a compelling indictment of Russia’s historical and present-day imperialism.

Sergio Fant

With thanks to German Films.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Minotaur

Andrey Zvyagintsev transposes Claude Chabrol’s La Femme infidèle to contemporary Russia, delivering a magnificent political allegory that dissects the mechanics of ego, violence and corruption.

My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile

The second part of Julia Loktev’s epic documentary, detailing the persecution of journalists in Russia, follows her brave protagonists’ escape abroad following the country’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Once Upon a Time in Harlem

Filmed by William Greaves in 1972 and completed by his son David 50 years later, this is a rapturous love letter to the Harlem Renaissance.

article_text:
Feature

Lula Victory Memes That Make Us All Want to Be Brazilian

Images rooted in queer and pop culture and national pride celebrate a progressive win at the polls and a step back for fascism.

Teletubbies ! (screenshot

Hyperallergic via

Instagram )

After an eye-opening loss during the first round of elections earlier this month, incumbent Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, known mononymously as Lula, staged a major comeback yesterday evening, defeating rival far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro in a tight presidential race. In a stark rejection of the region's rightward pivot, Lula's victory has yielded a deluge of memes exemplifying Brazilian digital culture's embodiment of national pride and identity and its broader global influence across social media.

With nearly 52% of the votes, Lula's win marks the progressive politician's second consecutive term and fourth term overall as president. As a founding member of Brazil's Workers' Party, Lula has consistently demonstrated his allegiance to ending food insecurity, increasing environmental protections, advocating for Indigenous territories and sovereignty, advancing labor rights and social equity, funding the arts and culture sector, and reinforcing national commitment to democracy, among other aligned policies.

Senator Bolsonaro, son of far-right former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, who was convicted of criminal conspiracy and sentenced to 27 years in prison last year after trying to incite a coup over Lula's third-term win in 2022, has publicly refused to recognize Lula's victory after the election was called. Lula's comeback flouts the United States's aggressive intervention tactics in Brazil's political landscape, which escalated significantly after Donald Trump imposed a 50% import tariff on Brazilian goods in retaliation against the prosecution of President Bolsonaro.

Hyperallergic via

For Brazilians who headed to the polls in droves to vote for Lula, this win has sparked a new wave of online celebration and optimism. One of the nation's greatest cultural exports is its fast-paced digital sense of humor, which has spawned ubiquitously used memes from the “ Confused math lady ” to “ Please come to Brazil .” As a facet of free speech in response to the political landscape, Brazil's gloves-off meme culture has both supplemented the far-right effort of electing the senior Bolsonaro and relentlessly skewered his presidency .

article_text:
風景画を旅するように味わえる展覧会が各地で開催されています。その土地や時代の景色を見る・知るだけではなく、画家の心象や眼差しを感じ取ることができるのも、風景画の魅力の一つです。ぜひ展示室で、珠玉の風景の数々にじっくりと向き合ってみてはいかがでしょうか。

「フォンタネージ ― イタリアの光・心の風景」東京・三菱一号館美術館で2027年1月24日まで イタリア近代風景画の巨匠の画業を紹介

「テート美術館 ターナー展」東京・国立西洋美術館で10月24日から ターナーの「崇高」を現代から読み解く

「アルベール・マルケ展」SOMPO美術館で12月13日まで 「水辺の情景」に注目 親友・マティスが「我らの北斎」と絶賛した画家の魅力とは？

「歌川広重 江戸のベストアングル」東京国立博物館で12月20日まで 東海道五拾三次（10月25日まで）など広重の三大風景画シリーズを3期に分けて全点一挙公開

「アンドリュー・ワイエス展」あべのハルカス美術館で12月6日まで 没後初の日本国内回顧展、約100点で画家の記憶と精神世界をたどる

「浮世絵の風景画を楽しむ 広重＋北斎」兵庫・芦屋市立美術博物館で2027年1月17日まで

特別展「原安三郎コレクション 北斎×広重」秋田県立近代美術館で12月6日まで 北斎の富士や広重の東海道など誰もが知る著名な浮世絵に加えて初公開の肉筆画も

「日本画の窓―旅する風景」群馬・高崎市タワー美術館で12月20日まで 国内外の風景を題材とした作品を中心に日本画家の多彩なまなざしを紹介

「印象派の先駆者 ウジェーヌ・ブーダン展 ―瞬間の美学、光の探求」山梨県立美術館で11月3日まで 約100点で“空の王者”の魅力をたどる

「三岸節子 ヨーロッパを巡って 新収蔵作品とともに」愛知・一宮市三岸節子記念美術館で11月8日まで フランス、スペイン、 イタリアなどヨーロッパ各地を巡って描いた豊かな風景画など生涯の作品を紹介

（読売新聞美術展ナビ編集班）

News

Is Germany's Far-Right AfD Co-Opting Joseph Beuys?

Dozens of galleries from Düsseldorf and Cologne signed a letter condemning the anti-immigrant party's invocation of the postwar artist in promotions for an upcoming event.

More than 50 galleries across Düsseldorf and Cologne have signed a letter condemning the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party's Düsseldorf faction for allegedly referencing postwar conceptual artist and political activist Joseph Beuys and poet Heinrich Heine in the promotion of an upcoming cultural policy event.

The AfD event in question, “Cultural Policy From the Right,” is scheduled to take place in Düsseldorf on Monday, October 26, and consists of a walking tour of the city's arts and cultural venues followed by a topical lecture from the party's Bundestag (parliament) member Matthias Helferich.

(Hyperallergic has contacted several signatories and was not able to independently confirm any mention of Beuys on the AfD and AfD Düsseldorf websites.)

Considered one of the more radical party members, Helferich was elected to the Bundestag in 2021 and was temporarily expelled from the AfD's North Rhine-Westphalia state branch in 2025 after leaked chats showed that he described himself as “the friendly face of the Nazis” and said he wanted to play as “democratic Freisler” (referring to Nazi judge Roland Freisler, known for his abusive courtroom conduct and imposing the death penalty on thousands, including juveniles). The politician claimed those descriptions parodied his left-wing online critics.

Beuys (image copyright bpk, Ernst von Siemens Kunststiftung, Stiftung Museum Schloss Moyland, and Ute Klophaus; courtesy Zero One Film and Kino Lorber)

Helferich was also accused of dehumanizing immigrants because of an Instagram story he posted of a rear-view mirror decoration with a sentence roughly translating to “get those creatures out” and added the tag #remigration — the term for the mass deportation of migrants, listed as one of the key AfD policies on the party's website. His expulsion from the party was ultimately overturned in June 2026.

“Düsseldorf is a city whose cultural identity is characterized by openness, internationality, plurality, and the free exchange of diverse perspectives,” a section of the co-signed letter reads . “Art emerges where boundaries are questioned and where people engage in dialogue regardless of origin, religion, skin color, gender, or political stance.”
excerpt_original: Dozens of galleries from Düsseldorf and Cologne signed a letter condemning the anti-immigrant party's invocation of the postwar artist in promotions for an upcoming event.

article_text:
Film

Kid Cudi to Write, Direct, and Star as Basquiat in New Biopic

The rapper called his forthcoming film, "JEAN," a “love letter” to the late artist and ’80s New York in his announcement on October 21.

American rapper Kid Cudi took to Instagram this week to announce his hand in writing, directing, and starring in the forthcoming project JEAN, a biopic of late contemporary artist Jean-Michel Basquiat. Cudi called the film a “love letter to Jean, the 80s and NY city,” and said that production is set to begin next year.

Cudi added that he will portray Basquiat, stating that the late artist has served as an inspiration to his career throughout, and that it'll be the “biggest honor to tell his story in a way we haven't seen before.”

“This one im so proud of and excited about,” Cudi wrote in the caption accompanying the mockup promotional poster and several black-and-white photos of him as Basquiat in a large studio. “To write a film about someone who existed was a challenge, but it was a welcomed one. A lot of research, books, talks with people that knew him.”

The announcement of JEAN comes after Cudi publicized his own foray into visual art in recent months. The multi-hyphenate artist debuted his painting practice under the name Scotty Ramon in a group presentation at Art Cologne 2025, and held his inaugural solo exhibition , Echoes of the Past , at the Paris location of Ruttkowski;68 this January.

article_text:
Art Review

“Costume Art” Is a Bad Look for The Met

The exhibition shapes a fashion canon based less on historical relevance than on the interests of those in charge.

Hyperallergic )

For an exhibition with such a simple title, Costume Art at the Metropolitan Museum of Art is awfully confusing. It’s also fairly problematic, but let’s start with the confusing parts. The show pairs garments and art objects to accomplish the radical task of “reveal[ing] the inherent relationship between clothing and the body,” as the website concisely explains. The artworks are meant to demonstrate the clothed body’s presence across The Met’s collection, evidently establishing the Costume Institute as the museum’s beating heart.

So clothing and the body are related, a fact to which The Met’s artworks attest. This ridiculously broad proclamation is organized into body typologies, starting with “Naked and Nude Body.” Other sections include “Anatomical Body,” “Abstract Body,” “Aging Body,” “Mortal Body,” and “Epidermal Body.”

With around 200 garments filling the Costume Institute’s nearly 12,000-square-foot, Grand Hall-adjacent new Condé M. Nast Galleries, certain pairings do enable visitors to experience the objects “through the lens of fashion, so the art becomes embodied,” as the Costume Institute’s Curator in Charge Andrew Bolton told the Art Newspaper — diaphanous Grecian-style gowns coupled with ancient Greek vessels, for instance.

Many other correspondences come across as forced, superficial, or questionable. For example, clothing by Chet Lo, who offered fabric swatches and audio descriptions to people with blindness and vision disabilities for his Spring 2025 collection, is juxtaposed with Picasso’s painting “The Blind Man’s Meal” (1903), while a limestone votive ear with the inscription “I belong to a deaf person” (4th–3rd century BCE) accompanies a “Deaf Dysmorphia” ensemble (2023) by designer Justin Dougan-Leblanc, who is deaf. If inclusiveness is a priority, why not feature artists living with blindness and deafness — for instance, Emilie Louise Gossiaux and Christine Sun Kim? Could the constant selfies at the Lo-Picasso display be the answer? This space was once a gift shop..

Likewise, a section titled “Pregnant Body” includes several works by (cis) men, as does “Reclaimed Body.” The latter couples Michaela Stark’s body-binding outfit “Twisted” (2026) with a photograph by Hans Bellmer of one of his faceless, limbless poupée (doll) sculptures.
